checks: Checked 18f8d2b72265ccb5 §6, (13). Both width functions are concave on their stated intervals, are positive at every interior positive base and nonnegative at the endpoints, and D lies in C. Thus both are full-dimensional compact convex bodies.
The fit at z=0 forces b=0. At z=t²>0 the width ratio gives |T|≤1/(1−t/2). Letting t decrease to zero gives |T|≤1 independently of shear. The identity is feasible and attains determinant one.

Every point of D with positive base is strictly interior to C since z≤3/2<2 and its width is strictly smaller. A supporting functional at the origin applied to (t²,±t) gives a t²+|u|t≤0 for every sufficiently small positive t, hence u=0. All continuous contact tensors vanish.

The only positive integer trace of D is the length-one centered interval at z=1. The indicated full-dimensional slab of C contains exactly one integer base and has a length-two centered interval there. Its centroid is (1,0) and halfspace depth one half follows directly from one centered interval, with the boundary-counting convention for pure-base cuts. The mass and width ratio checks were independently replayed exactly.

overlap.comparison: Establishes exact retention on lattice fibers and says nothing about the determinant of ambient fits or between-base contact obstructions.
Gives an ambient realization procedure for exact mixed traces. It does not supply the parabolic ambient fitting maximum or the failure of its normalized ambient contact tensor.

readability: The example tests ambient fits of D and the actual extraction separately. The displayed slab has its own true centroid and normalized depth.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The shrinking positive-base widths force the identity to be an ambient determinant maximum. Its sole ambient contact has pure-base normal, while the one positive integer fiber admits an exact doubling.
